title: Capacity squeeze analysis for new LLM onboarding (Q1 2026)
content:
Purpose:
Quick, pragmatic capacity worksheet to estimate the global impact of onboarding a new LLM variant (codenamed "orca-lite-x13") that increases per-request KV cache pressure and slightly larger GPU memory residency. This is a working sheet used to decide: reserved capacity, regional placement, and short-term burst buffers.

Assumptions (baseline):
- Current stable traffic baseline (all models): 85k qps global (p95).
- Active model mix currently: 60% base-gen, 30% chat, 10% embeddings.
- Typical avg output seq len: 120 tokens for gen/chat; 40 tokens for embeddings.
- Current KV prefix cache hit rate: 28% overall.
- Current average KV per-request (active): 120 KB (shared across requests).
- GPU types: A100-40GB in us-west/us-east, H100-80GB in eu-west for Dedicated pools.
- Cost numbers are placeholder hourly list price proxies used for delta analysis only.

New model specifics (orca-lite-x13):
- Expected customer adoption ramp: 0.5% -> 8% of qps over 12 weeks (three scenarios below).
- Per-request KV working set grows by ~1.8x (predictive prompts + longer contexts) -> avg KV per-request 216 KB.
- GPU memory per hot replica + runtime overhead: increases from 28GB -> 34GB for A100 runtime path (quantized), 44GB on H100 path (float16 variant) if we keep richer KV caches pinned.
- Serving latency SLOs require 99th percentile tail < 350ms (so we prefer local region routing).

Scenarios (global):
- Conservative (slow adoption): new model reaches 2% of qps by week 6, 4% by week 12.
- Expected: 2% week2, 5% week6, 8% week12.
- Aggressive: 5% week2, 10% week6, 15% week12.

Per-region projection table (snapshot: expected, week6):
| region | baseline qps | model qps (8% global scaled by region share) | avg seq len | KV/request (KB) | total KV active (GB) | avg GPU mem/replica (GB) | replicas needed (est) | notes |
| us-west | 28,000 | 2,240 | 130 | 216 | 2,240 * 216KB * 0.6 active-window ~ 290 GB | 20 (A100 40GB, reserve) | hotspot: origin for west customers |
| us-east | 32,000 | 2,560 | 125 | 216 | ~330 GB | 22 | prefer reserved commit in Q2 |
| eu-west | 15,000 | 1,200 | 120 | 216 | ~120 GB | 8 (H100 origin variants) | KV eviction policy review needed |
| ap-southeast | 10,000 | 800 | 110 | 216 | ~65 GB | 6 | smaller pool, use burst to us-east if needed |

Notes on table calculations (quick):
- total KV active (GB) ~= region_model_qps * KV/request (KB) * TTL_seconds / 1024 / 1024. Using TTL_seconds=120 (working-window ~ 2 minutes) for short-lived prefix entries. The rough numbers above use a conservative TTL and 60% active-working-set factor (some requests share prefixes).
- replicas needed: estimate = ceil((region_qps * avg_lat_work / (gpu_throughput_tokens)) adjusted for batching). This sheet uses simplified rule: replica_mem_limit / per-replica-live-model-mem. Rough and deliberately conservative for planning.

Impact breakdown (delta vs baseline):
- KV cache: global incremental KV footprint (expected, week6) ~ 805 GB total across regions. This is material: previously KV cluster pool for prefix lookups was ~1.4 TB; onboarding this model increases working set by ~57%.
- GPU count: expected additional A100 replicas ~ +56 (global) in expected ramp (distributed); aggressive could need ~+120.
- Tail latency risk: if we host fewer replicas but increase batching for cost, p99 tails risk > 400ms for multi-sequence mixes.

Operational options and mitigations (ranked):
1) Immediate: reduce default KV TTL for this model's prefixes from 120s -> 45s for initial 4 weeks to limit working set growth. Low friction but increases backend lookups. Action: INFRA-2147 (rule change).
2) Medium: enable adaptive routing by region+tier; route lowest-traffic regions to quantized variant of model (orca-lite-x13-q8) to reduce GPU mem to 26GB. Action: MODEL-8076 + canary in us-east.
3) Medium: enable per-customer prefix dedupe before KV insertion (saves ~15-25% of KV bytes). Engineering spike required (github:rw-infra/kv-cache-sim#42).
4) Long: procure additional committed A100 capacity in us-east for Q2; target +60 A100-40GB reserved. Finance review required.

Quick cost delta (very rough):
- A100 reserved delta hourly (per GPU incremental): $1.8/hr (committed discount estimate). 60 GPUs -> $108/hr -> ~$77k/mo.
- KV storage incremental: 805 GB * (managed cache overhead factor 1.3) ~ 1.05 TB. Managed cache storage + io ops ~ $0.7/hr incremental across regions (~$500/mo) (note: placeholder).

Open questions / unknowns to resolve before sign-off:
- Confirm actual KV TTL observed for typical long-chat flows (SLO vs cost trade). Instrumentation ticket: INFRA-2189.
- Validate that quantized variant meets quality bar for top-5 customers (Sofia to run: MODEL-EVAL-902).
- Confirm burst capacity policy with cloud provider for ap-southeast (Diego owns).

Actions / next steps:
- Short term (this week): implement TTL experiment (Marcus/Arielle) + simulate 24h traffic in kv-cache-sim with expected ramp (Diego).
- Week 1: canary model in us-east with q8 quant variant (Sofia).
- Week 2-3: revisit reserved commit ask with Finance (if canary shows >5% sustained adoption in us-east).

Notes to self / rough checklist:
- add per-request KV delta histogram to perf dashboard (trace id tag)
- update rollout runbook: automatic fallback to smaller variant when KV working set > threshold
- document region fallback order: us-east -> us-west -> eu-west -> ap-southeast

Appendix: short sim extract (sample calculation)
- sample region: us-east; baseline qps 32k; model qps 2.56k; KV/request 216KB; TTL 120s.
  working_set_bytes ~= 2560 req/s * 216KB * 120s * 0.6 ~= 40,147,200 KB ~= 38.3 GB (active-window) -> my earlier table used a 3x multiplier for request overlap leading to ~330GB; reconcile: difference due to overlap factor and multiple prefixes per request; need more accurate sim.

Conclusion (working):
Onboarding orca-lite-x13 materially increases KV working set and modestly increases GPU replica counts. We can buy time with TTL tuning and routing to quantized variants; strategic reserved procurement should be considered if adoption follows expected or aggressive ramps. This sheet is intentionally conservative — use the sim artifacts linked above to produce final commit ask to Finance.

-- end of working sheet --
